evaluations.evidence: search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting
evaluations.rationale: “Content identification” and “fingerprinting” can mean materially different techniques/scope (audio fingerprinting vs metadata matching vs watermarking), leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: based on my profile
evaluations.rationale: “Profile” is underspecified (listening history, demographics, preferences, explicit settings), allowing different implementations and data requirements.

evaluations.evidence: based on other users similar to myself
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is vague (similar taste, behavior, demographics, location), yielding materially different similarity models and outputs.

evaluations.evidence: similar ... based on content similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Similar”/“content similarity” is unclear (audio similarity, visual similarity, metadata similarity; whole video vs segments), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: exploiting enriched metadata and image tags ... other relevant listening path
evaluations.rationale: “Enriched metadata,” “image tags,” and “relevant listening path” are broad abstractions that can be interpreted in multiple materially different ways.

evaluations.evidence: upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps
evaluations.rationale: “Tags” (format, schema, source) and “all further processing steps” are undefined, leading to different scope/propagation requirements.

evaluations.evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
evaluations.rationale: “Thumbnail sequences” and what constitutes a “video segment” (fixed length, shot boundaries, user-defined) are unclear, affecting UI and segmentation logic.

evaluations.evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Info” and “similar” are unspecified (what attributes, what similarity basis), allowing materially different outputs and ranking behavior.

evaluations.evidence: info about perceptually similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Perceptually similar” is ambiguous (visual-only vs audio-visual; human perception model), leading to different similarity definitions.

evaluations.evidence: content recommendations from similar profiles
evaluations.rationale: Both “content” (type/scope) and “similar profiles” are vague, enabling different recommendation targets and similarity criteria.

evaluations.evidence: based on most relevant news events in my area
evaluations.rationale: “Most relevant,” “news events,” and “my area” are underspecified (radius, location source, relevance signals), yielding different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” could mean detect faces vs recognize specific individuals; “related information” is undefined, leading to different functional scope.

evaluations.evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify products” could mean generic product category detection vs specific SKU/brand recognition; “related information” is unclear.

evaluations.evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” may mean detect presence vs recognize which broadcaster; “related information” is unspecified, allowing different outputs.

evaluations.evidence: identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify brands” could mean logo detection, text recognition, or inferred brand association; “related information” is undefined.

evaluations.evidence: recommended with videos related to that picture or image
evaluations.rationale: “Related” is vague (visual similarity, same object, same topic, same location), leading to materially different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: access content using a geographical map ... videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest
evaluations.rationale: “Content,” “covering the area,” and “relevant point of interest” are unclear (coverage definition, POI criteria), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: search content items using automatic speech recognition
evaluations.rationale: “Search” via ASR is underspecified (search transcripts, keywords, speaker, language handling), and “content items” scope is unclear.

evaluations.evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation” is ambiguous (shots, scenes, chapters, time intervals) and “validate” criteria are unspecified, leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
evaluations.rationale: “Annotate” and “topic” are underspecified (taxonomy vs free text; single vs multiple topics), allowing materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
evaluations.rationale: “A/V quality aspects” is vague (resolution, bitrate, loudness, artifacts, sync), leading to different ranking/filter criteria.

evaluations.evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
evaluations.rationale: “Quick assessment” and “edited” are ambiguous (any processing vs specific edits; confidence threshold), yielding different detection requirements.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter nudity content
evaluations.rationale: “Nudity content” is undefined (partial nudity, artistic nudity, thresholds), leading to materially different filtering behavior.

evaluations.evidence: search based on low­level asset information
evaluations.rationale: “Low-level asset information” is an abstraction that can mean many different features/metadata, causing different interpretations of search criteria.

evaluations.evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
evaluations.rationale: “Validated” and “copyright infringement” detection scope are unclear (audio/video matching, thresholds, jurisdictions), enabling different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: high­level asset information such as metadata and tags either recognized by the system of provided by the user
evaluations.rationale: “High-level asset information” and “recognized by the system” are vague; also unclear which metadata/tags and how they are used for search/prefiltering.

evaluations.evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting,” “appealing,” and “complex” are subjective and can be operationalized in many materially different ways.

evaluations.evidence: detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should be prompted” and what constitutes a “subject”/trigger condition are unclear, allowing different alerting rules and thresholds.

evaluations.evidence: identify volunteer types
evaluations.rationale: “Volunteer types” is undefined (skill level, engagement segments, demographics, roles), leading to different classification schemes.

evaluations.evidence: preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassify” target classes and “simple low-level image features” are underspecified, enabling different feature sets and outputs.

evaluations.evidence: no classifiable animals
evaluations.rationale: “Classifiable animals” is ambiguous (no animals at all vs animals present but not identifiable; depends on taxonomy/quality thresholds).

evaluations.evidence: automatic image series detection ... timestamping malfunction
evaluations.rationale: “Image series detection” and what qualifies as “timestamping malfunction” are unclear, leading to different detection logic and outputs.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal species preclassification
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassification” is unclear (top-N suggestions vs hard labels; confidence thresholds; which species set), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal attribute preclassification
evaluations.rationale: “Attribute” is undefined (age, sex, behavior, markings, etc.) and “preclassification” output form is unclear.

evaluations.evidence: animal number detection
evaluations.rationale: “Number detection” is ambiguous (exact count vs range; handling occlusion/partial animals), leading to different functional expectations.

evaluations.evidence: automatic segmentation or localization of plankton
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation” vs “localization” are different outputs and the story allows either, creating materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: no classifiable plankton
evaluations.rationale: “Classifiable plankton” is unclear (none present vs present but too small/blurred; depends on class set/quality thresholds).

evaluations.evidence: detection of plankton size or orientation
evaluations.rationale: “Size” (which measure/units) and “orientation” (angle definition, reference axis) are underspecified; “or” allows different scopes.

evaluations.evidence: preclassification of plankton species
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassification” output and the species taxonomy are not specified, allowing different materially different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: worm motion analysis to reduce video duration
evaluations.rationale: “Reduce video duration” is ambiguous (speed-up, trimming inactive segments, summarization), leading to different processing requirements.

evaluations.evidence: detect the time ... where the worm lays an egg
evaluations.rationale: “The time” could mean timestamp of first frame, interval, or event time; egg-laying definition/criteria are not specified.

evaluations.evidence: detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc
evaluations.rationale: “Important features” is vague and the “etc” leaves scope open-ended, enabling materially different detection targets.

evaluations.evidence: assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience
evaluations.rationale: “Probability/weight” and “experience” are undefined (tenure, accuracy, volume), leading to different scoring models and usage.

evaluations.evidence: remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors
evaluations.rationale: “Artefacts” and “remove” are ambiguous (masking vs deletion vs correction; what counts as artefact vs real signal like bright stars).

evaluations.evidence: detect moving and transient objects
evaluations.rationale: “Moving” and “transient” are not operationally defined (time window, thresholds), allowing different detection criteria and outputs.

evaluations.evidence: remove background noise and distracting sounds
evaluations.rationale: “Background noise” and especially “distracting sounds” are subjective/underspecified, leading to different filtering targets and aggressiveness.

evaluations.evidence: group whale calls that are similar
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is vague (frequency patterns, duration, species, call type), enabling materially different grouping/clustering behavior.

evaluations.evidence: identify the number of whales heard
evaluations.rationale: “Number of whales heard” is ambiguous (distinct individuals vs overlapping calls; confidence/uncertainty handling), leading to different outputs.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should interrupt a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Should interrupt” is vague (which triggers, timing, frequency), allowing materially different intervention policies.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Criteria for choosing text vs image vs video are unspecified; “interrupt” context and decision rules are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should educate a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Educate” and when it “should” happen are underspecified (topics, triggers, cadence), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Decision criteria for modality selection are unclear; “educate” content/scope is not defined.

evaluations.evidence: know which piece of education I should give to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Piece of education” is undefined (lesson, hint, tutorial, FAQ item) and selection criteria are unclear, allowing different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: interesting comment
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting” is subjective and can be defined in many materially different ways (novelty, sentiment, scientific value).

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should comment” and “subject” are unclear (what triggers, what content, where), enabling different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should give an explanation
evaluations.rationale: “Explanation” and when it “should” be given are underspecified (type, length, trigger conditions), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: know what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “What ... should say” is open-ended without constraints (tone, content, context), leading to many materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: group subjects by similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Subjects” and “similarity” are undefined (similar images, metadata, classifications, discussion), enabling different grouping criteria.

evaluations.evidence: recommend different projects ... based on their previous experiences
evaluations.rationale: “Previous experiences” is vague (projects joined, performance, interests, time spent), leading to different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them
evaluations.rationale: “Summary” (length/type) and “articles” (which sources/types) are unclear; “reuse them” is also ambiguous (republish, reference, template).
